items.title: Microbial Identification by MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry: Sample Preparation
path: Microbial Identification by MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry: Sample Preparation

items.title: Introduction
items.text:
This procedure describes the sample preparation for the identification of bacteria, yeast, and filamentous fungi by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization – time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF).

This course encompasses the standard operating procedure (SOP) for spectra acquisition for microbial identification using MALDI-TOF MS.
path: Microbial Identification by MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry: Sample Preparation

items.title: Learning outcomes
items.text:
At the end of this course, you will be able to:

  • Identify and select the materials and reagents needed to prepare samples (bacteria, yeast, and filamentous fungi) for identification using MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry
  • Prepare reagents needed for the assay
  • Perform sample preparation for yeast and filamentous fungi using solid culture media
  • Perform sample preparation for filamentous fungi using liquid media
  • Perform sample preparation for bacteria using solid and liquid culture media
  • Prepare the MALDI-TOF MS target plate
  • If applicable: clean reusable MALDI-TOF target plates
path: Microbial Identification by MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry: Sample Preparation

items.title: Abbreviations
items.text:
• BTS — Bacterial Test Standard (Bruker)
  • HCCA — α-cyano-4-hydroxy-cinnamic acid
  • MALDI-TOF MS — Matrix Assisted Laser Desorption Ionization Time-Of-Flight Mass Spectrometry
  • TFA — Trifluoroacetic acid
path: Microbial Identification by MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry: Sample Preparation

items.title: Health & safety
items.text:
• Wear a lab coat and gloves during the practical work.
  • Work in a microbial biosafety cabinet (vertical laminar flow).
  • For the cleaning of reusable MALDI-TOF target plates: work in a chemical fume hood — TFA is very corrosive.
path: Microbial Identification by MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry: Sample Preparation

items.title: Equipment
items.text:
• MALDI-TOF mass spectrometer (e.g. Bruker Sirius)
  • MALDI-TOF MS target plate (if applicable, with adapter)
  • Microbial biosafety cabinet
  • Chemical fume hood
  • Centrifuge
  • Vortex
  • Micropipettes
path: Microbial Identification by MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry: Sample Preparation

items.title: Consumables
items.text:
• Microtubes (1.5 ml, sterile). Avoid tubes with surface treatment (e.g. silicone).
  • Falcon tubes (50 ml, sterile)
  • Disposable Pasteur pipettes (sterile)
  • Tips for micropipettes
  • Plastic forceps or loops (sterile)
  • Ethanol (absolute or analytical grade, non-denatured)
  • Formic acid (analytical grade)
  • Acetonitrile (analytical grade)
  • HCCA matrix — prepared following manufacturer's instructions
  • Calibration standard solution (e.g. Bruker BTS) — prepared following manufacturer's instructions
  • Ultrapure (e.g. MilliQ) water (sterile)
  • Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA)
  • Acetone
  • Precision wipes (for delicate tasks)
path: Microbial Identification by MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry: Sample Preparation

items.title: Solutions to prepare
items.text:
70% ethanol solution Mix 35 ml of absolute ethanol and 15 ml of ultrapure water in a 50 ml Falcon tube.

70% formic acid solution Place 15 ml of ultrapure water in a 50 ml Falcon tube and add 35 ml of formic acid. Mix gently.

80% TFA solution Place 5 ml of ultrapure water in a 50 ml Falcon tube and add 20 ml of TFA. Mix gently.

Once you're comfortable with the safety requirements, equipment, and solutions above, mark this module complete and continue to the sample preparation procedures.
path: Microbial Identification by MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry: Sample Preparation

items.title: Sample Preparation for Yeast and Filamentous Fungi
path: Sample Preparation for Yeast and Filamentous Fungi

items.title: Using solid culture media
path: Sample Preparation for Yeast and Filamentous Fungi

items.title: Culture
items.text:
• Culture the strains on a suitable solid culture medium (Petri dishes) at optimal growth temperature (usually 25–28°C). Seed the agar surface at several points to maximize growth.
  • Incubate for 2 days (yeast) or 3 days (filamentous fungi) at 25°C. If the growth is too limited after 3 days, extend the incubation until sufficient material is available to perform an extraction.
path: Sample Preparation for Yeast and Filamentous Fungi

items.title: Protein extraction
items.text:
1. Prepare pre-labelled 1.5 ml microtubes containing 300 µl of sterile water, one tube per culture.
  2. Using sterile forceps or loops, gently scrape the surface of the culture to collect yeast cells (or spores and mycelium for filamentous fungi), taking care not to remove any culture medium. Aim to collect an amount roughly the size of a lentil (young material from the outer edge of the colony).
  3. Transfer the collected material into the microtube containing sterile water.
  4. Vortex the tube shortly and add 900 µl of absolute ethanol.
  5. Vortex gently and centrifuge at 13,000 g for 10 minutes (this time can be reduced — the goal is a pellet that won't fall apart in the next step).
  6. Remove the supernatant by pipetting or decanting.
  7. Centrifuge again briefly (1–2 minutes) at 13,000 g.
  8. Remove the residual supernatant by pipetting and let the pellet air-dry for approximately 5–15 minutes.

Note: the pellet should be dried until no excess drops are visible on the tube surface. A damp pellet is acceptable. Too much residual ethanol reduces extraction efficiency through dilution; an overdried pellet becomes solid and hard to resuspend in formic acid, which also reduces efficiency.

  1. Once the pellet is dried, add 50 µl of 70% formic acid, vortex gently, and incubate for a maximum of 5 minutes at room temperature.
  2. Vortex and add 50 µl of acetonitrile, vortex gently, and incubate for a maximum of 5 minutes at room temperature.

Note: you can vary the volume of formic acid and acetonitrile (e.g. 30 µl instead of 50 µl for a more concentrated extract), but the formic acid volume must always equal the acetonitrile volume. A very small pellet needs 10–20 µl; a large pellet can need up to 80 µl. The added volume should just cover the pellet.

Troubleshooting: if spectra acquisition is repeatedly unsuccessful, bead beating can be performed during the formic acid incubation.

  1. Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 13,000 g. The supernatant is the final extract. Store the extract at -20°C until further analysis.
path: Sample Preparation for Yeast and Filamentous Fungi

items.title: Using liquid culture media (filamentous fungi)
path: Sample Preparation for Yeast and Filamentous Fungi

items.title: Culture
items.text:
• Inoculate the liquid cultivation tubes (e.g. Sabouraud Dextrose Broth) with the biological material and close the lid. For sporulating fungi, use a wetted cotton swab to collect spores by touching the sporulating surface once. For non-sporulating fungi, collect a small amount of young mycelium.
  • Place the tubes in the rotator incubator and incubate at 25°C overnight, or until sufficient biological material is observed. Liquid cultivation is faster than solid — one to two days is usually enough.
path: Sample Preparation for Yeast and Filamentous Fungi

items.title: Protein extraction
items.text:
1. Remove the cultivation tubes from the rotator, place them on the bench, and let the biological material settle for 1–60 minutes depending on the species.
  2. Harvest 1500 µl from the sediment into a pre-labelled 1.5 ml microtube using a disposable Pasteur pipette.
  3. Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 13,000 g and remove the supernatant with a micropipette.

Note: centrifuge an extra 3 minutes if the pellet isn't well defined. If that doesn't help, remove as much medium as possible, add 100–300 µl ethanol to improve pellet formation, centrifuge again for 3 minutes, and remove the supernatant. If the pellet is too small but the supernatant is clear, add more biological material and repeat.

  1. Add 1 ml of ultrapure water, vortex, and centrifuge for 2 minutes at 13,000 g.
  2. Carefully remove the supernatant, add another 1 ml of ultrapure water, and vortex to resuspend the pellet.
  3. Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 13,000 g and repeat the previous water-wash step.
  4. Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 13,000 g and remove the supernatant.
  5. Add 300 µl of ultrapure water to the pellet and resuspend by pipetting up and down.
  6. Add 900 µl of ethanol and pipette up and down.
  7. Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 13,000 g, remove the supernatant, then centrifuge again briefly (1–2 minutes) and remove any residual supernatant.
  8. Let the pellet air-dry for approximately 5–15 minutes (same drying guidance as above — a damp pellet is fine, an overdried one is not).
  9. Add 50 µl of 70% formic acid, vortex, incubate up to 5 minutes; then add 50 µl of acetonitrile, vortex, incubate up to 5 minutes (same volume-adjustment rule as above).
  10. Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 13,000 g. The supernatant is the final extract. Store at -20°C until further analysis.
path: Sample Preparation for Yeast and Filamentous Fungi

items.title: Culture
items.text: Culture the bacterial strains on the appropriate solid culture medium for 6 to 48h at optimal growth temperature. If growth is too limited after 48h, extend the incubation until sufficient material is available to perform an extraction.

items.title: Protein extraction
items.text:
1. In a 1.5 ml microtube, resuspend bacteria (from a single colony up to the size of a lentil) in 1 ml of ultrapure water.
  2. Centrifuge at 13,000 g for 2 minutes and discard the supernatant.
  3. Resuspend the pellet in 300 µl of ultrapure water and add 900 µl of ethanol. Mix gently by pipetting or vortexing.
  4. Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 13,000 g.
  5. Remove the supernatant by pipetting or decanting.
  6. Centrifuge again briefly (1–2 minutes) at 13,000 g and remove the residual supernatant.
  7. Let the pellet air-dry for approximately 5–15 minutes.
  8. Once dried, add 40 µl of 70% formic acid and vortex gently (a compact pellet can be fragmented with the pipette tip while adding the acid).
  9. Add 40 µl of acetonitrile and vortex gently.

Note: you can vary the formic acid / acetonitrile volume between 10 and 80 µl, but the two volumes must always be equal. A very small pellet needs 10–20 µl; a large pellet can need up to 80 µl. The added volume should just cover the pellet.

  1. Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 13,000 g. The supernatant is the final extract. Store at -20°C until further analysis.

items.title: Culture
items.text: Inoculate the liquid cultivation tubes with the biological material and close the lid. Incubate for 7h to overnight at optimal growth temperature. If growth is slow, extend the incubation until sufficient material is available.

items.title: Protein extraction
items.text:
1. Transfer 1 ml of the liquid culture into a 1.5 ml microtube.
  2. Centrifuge at 13,000 g for 2 minutes and discard the supernatant.
  3. Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of ultrapure water, centrifuge again at 13,000 g for 2 minutes, and discard the supernatant.
  4. Resuspend the pellet in 300 µl of ultrapure water and add 900 µl of ethanol. Mix gently by pipetting or vortexing.
  5. Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 13,000 g.
  6. Remove the supernatant by pipetting or decanting.
  7. Centrifuge again briefly (1–2 minutes) at 13,000 g and remove the residual supernatant.
  8. Let the pellet air-dry for approximately 5–15 minutes.
  9. Once dried, add 40 µl of 70% formic acid and vortex gently.
  10. Add 40 µl of acetonitrile and vortex gently (same volume-adjustment rule as the solid-media protocol).
  11. Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 13,000 g. The supernatant is the final extract. Store at -20°C until further analysis.

items.title: Preparation of the MALDI-TOF Target Plate
items.text:
1. Place 1 µl of the final extract onto a sample spot of the MALDI-TOF target plate. Foresee one spot with the BTS (calibration and positive control).
  2. Let the extracts and BTS dry completely at room temperature. For faster drying, use an elevated temperature (35°C) or a manufacturer device such as the Bruker MBT FAST Shuttle.

Note: for identification, analyse the extracts in replicates (2 to 4 spots per extract) to check for consistency of the identification results.

Note: to create a sample reference spectrum, a minimum of 8 replicates is required, each shot 3 times, for a total minimum of 24 spectra.

  1. Add 1 µl of HCCA matrix to overlay the spots with dried extracts or BTS. Foresee one spot with HCCA matrix only (no extract or BTS) as a negative control, to verify the matrix alone produces no peaks.
  2. Let the HCCA matrix dry completely (same procedure as for the extract).

The plate is then ready to be analysed.

Note: once a sample extract has dried, the HCCA matrix must be added within 30 minutes. Prepared MALDI-TOF target plates must be analysed within 24h.
path: Preparation of the MALDI-TOF Target Plate

items.title: Cleaning of Reusable MALDI-TOF Target Plates
items.text:
Safety reminder: work in a chemical fume hood — TFA is very corrosive.

  1. Soak the plate in 70% ethanol for five minutes.
  2. Rinse the plate with tap water and dry with a precision wipe.
  3. Rinse the plate with acetone and dry with a precision wipe.
  4. Rinse the plate with 70% ethanol and dry with a precision wipe.
  5. Rinse the plate with tap water and dry with a precision wipe.
  6. Place 100 µl of 80% TFA and spread it onto the entire surface of the plate with a pipette tip, loop, or wipe (rubbing the surface with the wipe).
  7. Dry the plate with a precision wipe.
  8. Rinse the plate with ultrapure water and dry with a precision wipe.
  9. Let the plate dry completely for 10–20 minutes in the open air.

This step applies only if your target plates are reusable — disposable plates do not require this procedure.
path: Cleaning of Reusable MALDI-TOF Target Plates
